select
    id as conversation_id,
    organization_id,
    -- Normalize channel enums so MetricFlow group_by/filters stay consistent.
    case
        when lower(coalesce(channel, '')) in ('web_chat', 'webchat') then 'webchat'
        when lower(coalesce(channel, '')) in ('voice', 'call') then 'voice'
        else lower(channel)
    end as channel,
    direction,
    contact_id,
    profile_id,
    queue_id,
    assigned_agent_id,
    status,
    priority,
    lifecycle_state,
    sla_status,
    handoff_reason,
    disposition_code,
    resolution_code,
    created_at,
    queued_at,
    assigned_at,
    first_response_at,
    resolved_at,
    closed_at,
    ended_at,

    -- proxy flag: conversation stayed AI-only, no human ever assigned/handed to,
    -- and reached a terminal state. lifecycle_state is always 'ended' in prod
    -- (never 'bot'/'agent'/'human') so it cannot be used as a signal here.
    case
        when handoff_reason is null
         and assigned_agent_id is null
         and (status in ('resolved', 'closed') or closed_at is not null)
        then true
        else false
    end as is_ai_only_completed,

    -- proxy flag: a handoff to a human was ever requested (does not imply completion)
    (handoff_reason is not null) as had_handoff,

    -- handled = reached a terminal outcome by ANY means, bot or human.
    -- Do NOT use handoff_reason here — it only means a handoff was requested,
    -- not that the conversation was actually handled by anyone.
    case
        when assigned_agent_id is not null
          or status in ('resolved', 'closed')
          or closed_at is not null
        then true
        else false
    end as is_handled,

    case
        when status = 'resolved' or resolution_code is not null or resolved_at is not null
        then true
        else false
    end as is_resolved,

    case when first_response_at is not null and created_at is not null
        then extract(epoch from (first_response_at - created_at))
    end as first_response_seconds,

    case when assigned_at is not null and queued_at is not null
        then extract(epoch from (assigned_at - queued_at))
    end as speed_of_answer_seconds,

    -- Queue-depth snapshot: terminal statuses are resolved/closed (not a literal 'open').
    (status not in ('resolved', 'closed')) as is_open

from "worktual_bigint"."ccass"."conversations"

-- Agent-assist suggestion proxy. Real schema only has a boolean `accepted`,
-- not a full accepted/modified/rejected enum, so we infer:
--   accepted = true  and final_text = suggestion_text  -> 'accepted'
--   accepted = true  and final_text != suggestion_text -> 'modified'
--   accepted = false                                    -> 'rejected'
--   accepted is null                                    -> 'pending'
select
    id as suggestion_id,
    organization_id,
    session_id,
    conversation_id,
    skill_key,
    accepted,
    suggestion_text,
    final_text,
    status,
    created_at,

    case
        when accepted is true and final_text is not distinct from suggestion_text then 'accepted'
        when accepted is true and final_text is distinct from suggestion_text then 'modified'
        when accepted is false then 'rejected'
        else 'pending'
    end as suggestion_disposition

from "worktual_bigint"."ccass"."copilot_turns"

-- performance across A/B variants and delivery platforms within a campaign.
-- Same proxy caveats as mart_campaign_touch_performance: is_sent_flag = 'sent' status
-- stands in for "delivered"; no conversion field exists in the source schema.
with recipients as (

),

campaigns as (

    r.campaign_id,
    c.organization_id,
    c.campaign_created_at,
    coalesce(r.ab_variant, 'none')            as ab_variant,
    coalesce(r.recipient_platform, 'unknown') as recipient_platform,
    count(*)                                as touch_count,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_sent_flag)     as sent_touch_count,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_failed_flag)    as failed_touch_count,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_opened_flag)    as opened_touch_count,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_clicked_flag)   as clicked_touch_count,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_opened_flag)::numeric
        / nullif(count(*) filter (where r.is_sent_flag), 0)  as open_rate,
    count(*) filter (where r.is_clicked_flag)::numeric
        / nullif(count(*) filter (where r.is_sent_flag), 0)  as click_rate
from recipients r
left join campaigns c on c.campaign_id = r.campaign_id
group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

-- Grain: campaign_id. Proxy for campaign_touch_volume, delivery_rate, open_rate,
-- click_rate, failure_rate, frequency_per_contact.
-- CAVEAT: no literal "delivered" status exists on the source table — is_sent_flag
-- (status='sent') is used as the delivery proxy. No conversion field exists anywhere
-- in the schema, so conversion_rate / converted_touch_count are NOT built here.
with recipients as (
    select * from "worktual_bigint"."campaign_staging"."stg_campaign_send_recipients"
),

campaigns as (
    select campaign_id, organization_id, created_at as campaign_created_at
    from "worktual_bigint"."campaign_staging"."stg_campaigns"
),

per_campaign as (
    select
        campaign_id,
        count(*)                                   as touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where is_sent_flag)        as sent_touch_count,      -- delivery proxy
        count(*) filter (where is_failed_flag)       as failed_touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where is_skipped_flag)      as skipped_touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where is_opened_flag)       as opened_touch_count,
        count(*) filter (where is_clicked_flag)      as clicked_touch_count,
        count(distinct contact_id)                  as unique_contacts_touched,
        avg(attempt_count)                          as avg_attempt_count,
        avg(seconds_to_open)                        as avg_seconds_to_open,
        avg(seconds_open_to_click)                  as avg_seconds_open_to_click
    from recipients
    group by 1
)

select
    p.campaign_id,
    c.organization_id,
    c.campaign_created_at,
    touch_count,
    sent_touch_count,
    failed_touch_count,
    skipped_touch_count,
    opened_touch_count,
    clicked_touch_count,
    unique_contacts_touched,
    avg_attempt_count,
    avg_seconds_to_open,
    avg_seconds_open_to_click,
    -- ratio metrics computed here (mart layer) since they need cross-column division
    -- Postgres: guard divide-by-zero with nullif()
    sent_touch_count::numeric    / nullif(touch_count, 0)             as delivery_rate,      -- proxy: sent / total
    opened_touch_count::numeric  / nullif(sent_touch_count, 0)        as open_rate,
    clicked_touch_count::numeric / nullif(sent_touch_count, 0)        as click_rate,
    failed_touch_count::numeric  / nullif(touch_count, 0)             as failure_rate,
    touch_count::numeric         / nullif(unique_contacts_touched, 0) as frequency_per_contact
from per_campaign p
left join campaigns c on c.campaign_id = p.campaign_id

-- Grain: organization_id. Proxy for unsubscribe_rate and suppression_rate.
-- CAVEAT: both source tables are org-level, not per-campaign or per-touch — the metrics
-- doc defines these at campaign_touch grain, which doesn't exist. This mart answers
-- "what share of an org's known contacts/emails are unsubscribed or suppressed",
-- not "what share of touches on campaign X caused an unsubscribe".
with engagement as (
    select
        organization_id,
        min(created_at)                             as first_engagement_at,
        count(*)                                   as engaged_contact_count,
        count(*) filter (where email_unsubscribed)  as unsubscribed_contact_count
    from "worktual_bigint"."campaign_staging"."stg_campaign_contact_engagement"
    group by 1
),

suppressions as (
    select
        organization_id,
        count(*)                                       as suppressed_email_count,
        count(*) filter (where suppression_reason = 'unsub')       as unsub_suppressed_count,
        count(*) filter (where suppression_reason = 'hard_bounce') as bounce_suppressed_count,
        count(*) filter (where suppression_reason = 'complaint')   as complaint_suppressed_count
    from "worktual_bigint"."campaign_staging"."stg_email_suppressions"
    group by 1
)

select
    coalesce(e.organization_id, s.organization_id) as organization_id,
    e.first_engagement_at,
    e.engaged_contact_count,
    e.unsubscribed_contact_count,
    e.unsubscribed_contact_count::numeric / nullif(e.engaged_contact_count, 0) as unsubscribe_rate,
    s.suppressed_email_count,
    s.unsub_suppressed_count,
    s.bounce_suppressed_count,
    s.complaint_suppressed_count,
    -- rate proxies: share of an org's total suppressions attributable to each cause
    -- (NOT a bounce/complaint rate against total sends — no per-send bounce/complaint
    -- field exists anywhere in the schema, so "of everything sent" is not buildable)
    s.bounce_suppressed_count::numeric    / nullif(s.suppressed_email_count, 0) as bounce_share_of_suppressions,
    s.complaint_suppressed_count::numeric / nullif(s.suppressed_email_count, 0) as complaint_share_of_suppressions,
    s.suppressed_email_count::numeric     / nullif(e.engaged_contact_count, 0)  as suppression_rate
from engagement e

-- status-driven terminal flag, org attributes, and SLA target hours by
-- priority — so metrics can be grouped/filtered on all of these directly
-- without a query-time join.
select
    t.ticket_id,
    t.organization_id,
    o.organization_name,
    o.business_type             as organization_business_type,
    t.ticket_number,
    t.subject,
    t.status,
    ts.status_display_name,
    ts.is_terminal               as is_closed_by_status,
    t.priority,
    t.channel,
    t.customer_id,
    t.customer_name,
    t.customer_email,
    c.account_id,
    a.account_name,
    t.assignee_id,
    t.assignee_name,
    u.role                      as assignee_role,
    t.resolver_id,
    t.resolver_name,
    t.queue_id,
    t.queue_name,
    q.queue_type,
    q.sla_status                as queue_sla_status,
    true                        as team_supports_ticketing,
    t.category,
    t.skill,
    t.due_at,
    t.first_response_at,
    t.resolved_at,
    t.csat_score,
    t.csat_rated_at,
    t.created_by_id,
    t.created_by_name,
    -- Column order matches the live view so CREATE OR REPLACE is valid.
    -- Flag values come from tickets.status (stg_*), never ticket_statuses.is_terminal.
    t.is_resolved,
    t.is_open,
    t.is_breached_proxy,
    t.resolution_hours,
    t.first_response_hours,
    case when t.first_response_at is not null
         then extract(epoch from (t.first_response_at - t.created_at)) / 60.0
    end                          as first_response_minutes,
    t.has_first_response,
    t.has_csat_score,
    case when t.assignee_id is not null and t.assignee_name is not null and t.assignee_name != 'Unassigned'
         then true else false end as has_assignee,
    case when t.resolver_id is not null or (t.resolver_name is not null and t.resolver_name != '')
         then true else false end as has_resolver,
    case when t.csat_score is not null then true else false end as has_csat_rating,
    case when t.is_pending
              and t.due_at is not null
              and t.due_at < now()
         then true else false end as is_overdue,
    case when lower(t.status) = 'reopened' then true else false end as is_reopened,
    t.is_pending,
    t.is_closed,
    case when t.is_open and lower(t.priority) = 'high'
         then true else false end as is_high_priority_open,
    case when t.is_pending and t.due_at is not null and date(t.due_at) = current_date
         then true else false end as is_due_today,
    case when t.is_pending
              and t.due_at is not null
              and date(t.due_at) = current_date
         then true else false end as is_sla_at_risk,
    case when t.resolved_at is not null and t.due_at is not null and t.resolved_at > t.due_at
         then extract(epoch from (t.resolved_at - t.due_at)) / 3600.0
    end                          as overdue_hours,
    case when t.resolved_at is not null and t.due_at is not null and t.resolved_at <= t.due_at then true
         when t.is_resolved and sp.resolution_hours is not null and t.resolution_hours <= sp.resolution_hours then true
         else false end          as is_resolution_sla_met,
    case when t.resolved_at is not null and (t.due_at is not null or sp.resolution_hours is not null)
         then true else false end as has_resolution_sla_target,
    -- SLA target hours by priority, for actual-vs-target comparison
    sp.resolution_hours          as sla_resolution_hours,
    sp.first_response_hours      as sla_first_response_hours,
    case when t.is_resolved and sp.resolution_hours is not null
         then t.resolution_hours - sp.resolution_hours
    end                          as resolution_hours_variance,
    t.created_at,
    t.updated_at
from "worktual_bigint"."ticketing_staging"."stg_tickets" t

-- One row per organization_id x day. Pre-aggregates funnel counts and
-- daily rates so `agg: average` measures can correctly average per-period
-- values (see mart_deal_daily_summary.sql for the same pattern/rationale).

select

    business_type,
    date_trunc('day', created_at)                                          as day,
    count(contact_id)                                                       as contact_count,
    count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','subscriber')
               then contact_id end)                                         as new_lead_count,
    count(case when is_mql_proxy then contact_id end)                       as mql_proxy_count,
    count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer')
               then contact_id end)                                         as eligible_lead_count,
    count(case when lifecycle_stage = 'customer' then contact_id end)       as customer_count,
    count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer','subscriber')
               then contact_id end)                                         as funnel_eligible_count,
    case when count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer')
                        then contact_id end) > 0
         then count(case when is_mql_proxy then contact_id end)::decimal
              / nullif(count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer')
                                  then contact_id end), 0)
    end                                                                     as daily_mql_rate,
    case when count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer','subscriber')
                        then contact_id end) > 0
         then count(case when lifecycle_stage = 'customer' then contact_id end)::decimal
              / nullif(count(case when lifecycle_stage in ('lead','mql','prospect','customer','subscriber')
                                  then contact_id end), 0)
    end                                                                     as daily_customer_conversion_rate

-- One row per organization_id x created_at day.
-- Pre-aggregates deal counts so `agg: average` measures in the semantic
-- layer can correctly average per-day (or rolled-up per-week/month/etc.)
-- values, instead of recomputing a ratio over the whole filtered range.

select
    organization_id,
    business_type,
    date_trunc('day', created_at)                          as day,
    count(deal_id)                                          as deal_count,
    sum(case when is_open then amount else 0 end)           as open_pipeline_amount,
    count(case when is_won then deal_id end)                as won_deal_count,
    count(case when is_lost then deal_id end)                as lost_deal_count,
    count(case when is_closed then deal_id end)               as closed_deal_count,
    -- daily win / loss rate, NULL (not 0) when nothing closed that day so
    -- AVG() correctly excludes no-activity days rather than dragging the
    -- average toward zero
    case when count(case when is_closed then deal_id end) > 0
         then count(case when is_won then deal_id end)::decimal
              / nullif(count(case when is_closed then deal_id end), 0)
    end                                                       as daily_win_rate,
    case when count(case when is_closed then deal_id end) > 0
         then count(case when is_lost then deal_id end)::decimal
              / nullif(count(case when is_closed then deal_id end), 0)
    end                                                       as daily_loss_rate
from "worktual_bigint"."crm_marts"."mart_deals"
group by 1, 2, 3

-- boolean flag and counted with count_distinct — MetricFlow ratio/simple

-- order grain, so that aggregation has to happen here instead.

    o.contact_id,
    o.organization_id,
    min(o.created_at)                as first_order_at,
    max(o.created_at)                as most_recent_order_at,
    count(distinct o.order_id)       as order_count,
    sum(o.total)                     as lifetime_order_value,
    case when count(distinct o.order_id) >= 2 then true else false end as is_repeat_customer

group by o.contact_id, o.organization_id
